source: The one-sentence `where` text for every lookup-kind row the Ledger (master prompt section 18.2) will need: which document or screen, and what to do if it is not there. Lane 2, section 4 (DECISIONS.md L-4). Written so a person can follow it on a phone.
confidenceNote: Directions, not figures. Site layouts change; each sentence names the document and the line, not a button position.
note: Shape follows section 18.2: `path` is the household path (a proposal until data/ledger-rows.json exists), `letter` the DAITE family, `kind` is always lookup here, `where` is the sentence, `ifMissing` says what to do when the document is not there, `roughly` says what to type for now. Under data/lane2/ until shared/reference.js registers it (docs/lane2-proposals.md P-5).

refresh.against: nothing external: re-read each sentence against a current statement once a year and fix any that no longer matches what the site shows.

rows.label: Checking balance
rows.where: Open your bank app; the number under the account name on the first screen is the balance.
rows.ifMissing: Log in on the bank website instead, or use the balance from your last text or email alert.
rows.roughly: What you think is in there today, to the nearest hundred.

rows.label: Savings balance
rows.where: Same bank app, the savings account line; if you have more than one, add them.
rows.ifMissing: Check the last monthly statement email from the bank.
rows.roughly: Round to the nearest hundred.

rows.label: Brokerage balance
rows.where: Open the brokerage app; the total at the top of the home screen is the account value including cash.
rows.ifMissing: The monthly statement PDF, first page, the line called total account value.
rows.roughly: The last number you remember, to the nearest thousand.

rows.label: 401(k) balance
rows.where: Log in to the plan website (the name on your pay stub, like Fidelity or Vanguard); the front page shows the total balance.
rows.ifMissing: Your HR benefits page links to it, and the quarterly statement in the mail has it on page one.
rows.roughly: Your last statement figure, to the nearest thousand.

rows.label: Traditional IRA balance
rows.where: Open the app of the company that holds it; the account list shows each balance beside its name.
rows.ifMissing: The year-end statement or the Form 5498 the company mails each spring shows the balance.
rows.roughly: To the nearest thousand.

rows.label: Roth IRA balance
rows.where: Same place as the other accounts at that company; the word Roth is in the account name.
rows.ifMissing: Form 5498 from that company, box 5 on the year-end statement.
rows.roughly: To the nearest thousand.

rows.label: HSA balance
rows.where: Log in to the HSA provider (the name on your HSA debit card); the home screen shows cash and invested balances, add both.
rows.ifMissing: Your health plan or HR benefits page links to the provider; the yearly Form 5498-SA has the balance.
rows.roughly: To the nearest hundred.

rows.label: 529 balance
rows.where: Log in to the state 529 plan site; the account balance is on the first screen after login.
rows.ifMissing: The quarterly statement email or the plan's mailed statement, first page.
rows.roughly: To the nearest thousand.

rows.label: Pension monthly amount
rows.where: The yearly pension statement from the employer or plan, the line called estimated monthly benefit at your normal retirement age.
rows.ifMissing: Call the plan's number on any letter from them and ask for a benefit estimate; HR can send the statement again.
rows.roughly: Type 0 if you are not sure you have one; the room will ask again.

rows.label: Home value
rows.where: The estimate on Zillow or Redfin for your address, or the county assessor's market value on your property tax bill.
rows.ifMissing: What a similar home on your street sold for recently, from the same sites.
rows.roughly: What you think it would sell for, to the nearest ten thousand.

rows.label: Car value
rows.where: Kelley Blue Book or Edmunds, the private party value for your year, model and mileage.
rows.ifMissing: A quick offer from Carvana or CarMax online gives a floor.
rows.roughly: To the nearest thousand.

rows.label: Credit card APR
rows.where: Your card statement, the box near the end called interest charge calculation; the purchase APR is the first line.
rows.ifMissing: In the card app, the card details or account terms page lists the purchase APR.
rows.roughly: Type 24% if you have no idea; most cards sit between 20% and 30%.

rows.label: Student loan interest rate
rows.where: Log in to studentaid.gov, My Aid, then View Loans; each loan lists its interest rate.
rows.ifMissing: Your servicer's site (the company that bills you) lists each loan's rate on the loan details page.
rows.roughly: Type 6% for federal loans from the last ten years.

rows.label: Car loan APR
rows.where: The loan statement or the lender's app, the line called annual percentage rate or interest rate.
rows.ifMissing: The signed loan contract from the dealer, first page, the box marked APR.
rows.roughly: Type 7% if the car is under two years old, 9% if older.

rows.label: Mortgage rate
rows.where: The monthly mortgage statement, near the top, the line called interest rate.
rows.ifMissing: The closing documents, the page called the Note, first paragraph.
rows.roughly: Type the rate you remember agreeing to.

rows.label: Personal loan APR
rows.where: The lender's app or statement, the loan details page, the line called APR.
rows.ifMissing: The loan agreement email from when you took it out.
rows.roughly: Type 12% if you have no idea.

rows.label: Loan or card balance
rows.where: The current balance on the lender's app home screen, or the statement balance on the latest statement.
rows.ifMissing: The lender's automated phone line reads the balance after you enter the account number.
rows.roughly: The last statement figure you remember.

rows.label: Minimum payment
rows.where: The latest statement, the line called minimum payment due, near the top.
rows.ifMissing: The lender's app shows it on the payment screen.
rows.roughly: For a card, 2% of the balance; for a loan, the fixed monthly payment.

rows.label: Take-home from a pay stub
rows.where: Your latest pay stub, the line called net pay; multiply by the number of paycheques in a year if the room asks for a yearly figure.
rows.ifMissing: The amount your bank shows landing from your employer on payday is the same number.
rows.roughly: About 70% of your gross pay.

rows.label: Employer match formula
rows.where: The plan website, the contributions or plan details page, a sentence like 100% of the first 3% and 50% of the next 2%.
rows.ifMissing: Ask HR for the summary plan description; the match is in the section called employer contributions.
rows.roughly: Type 50% up to 6% of pay, the most common formula.

rows.label: Vesting schedule
rows.where: The plan website, the vesting page, which shows the percent that is yours now and the schedule by year of service.
rows.ifMissing: The summary plan description from HR, under vesting.
rows.roughly: Type 100% if you have been there five years or more.

rows.label: Social Security estimate
rows.where: Log in at ssa.gov/myaccount; the front page shows your estimated monthly benefit at 62, full retirement age and 70.
rows.ifMissing: Create the account with your Social Security number; it takes ten minutes and the estimate appears at once.
rows.roughly: Type 40% of your current monthly gross pay as the full-age figure.

rows.label: Pension statement
rows.where: The yearly statement the plan mails or posts online, the line called accrued monthly benefit.
rows.ifMissing: The plan's member website has a benefit calculator; HR has the contact.
rows.roughly: Leave blank and mark roughly; the room will keep asking.

rows.label: Property tax bill
rows.where: The county assessor or treasurer website, search your address; the yearly bill total is on the tax bill page.
rows.ifMissing: Your mortgage statement's escrow section shows the yearly tax paid; the closing documents estimate it too.
rows.roughly: 1% of the home's value a year.

rows.label: Health insurance premium
rows.where: Your pay stub, the deduction line for medical or health; multiply by paycheques a month.
rows.ifMissing: For a marketplace plan, the monthly premium is on the healthcare.gov account home screen after any credit.
rows.roughly: Type 150 a month for job coverage, 450 for a marketplace plan.

rows.label: Auto insurance premium
rows.where: The declarations page the insurer emailed at renewal, the total premium for the policy period; divide by six or twelve for a month.
rows.ifMissing: The insurer's app shows the policy total on the policy screen.
rows.roughly: 200 a month per car.

rows.label: Home or renters insurance premium
rows.where: The declarations page from the insurer, the yearly premium line; homeowners often pay it through the mortgage escrow.
rows.ifMissing: The mortgage statement escrow section shows the yearly insurance paid.
rows.roughly: Renters 20 a month; homeowners 0.5% of the home value a year.

rows.label: Life insurance policy
rows.where: The policy document or the insurer's app, the face amount (what it pays) and the premium; job coverage is on the benefits page as a multiple of salary.
rows.ifMissing: HR benefits page lists the employer policy; a personal policy has a yearly statement.
rows.roughly: Type the multiple of salary your job gives, usually one or two times.

rows.label: Disability insurance
rows.where: The benefits page at work, long-term disability, which says what share of pay it replaces and after how many weeks.
rows.ifMissing: Ask HR for the benefits summary; a personal policy has the monthly benefit on page one.
rows.roughly: Type 60% of gross pay as the monthly benefit if you have job coverage.

rows.label: Student loan servicer and plan
rows.where: Log in to studentaid.gov; the dashboard names your servicer, and the servicer's site shows your repayment plan on the loan details page.
rows.ifMissing: The last letter or email about your loans names the servicer; call them for the plan name.
rows.roughly: Pick standard if you have never chosen a plan.

rows.label: RSU grant document
rows.where: The equity site (Schwab, Fidelity, Carta, Shareworks), the grants page; each grant shows shares, the vesting dates and how many have vested.
rows.ifMissing: The offer letter or grant agreement email has the share count and vesting schedule.
rows.roughly: Type the yearly value from your offer letter.

rows.label: HSA balance
rows.where: The HSA provider's app, home screen, cash balance plus investment balance.
rows.ifMissing: Form 5498-SA, mailed each spring, box 5.
rows.roughly: To the nearest hundred.

rows.label: 529 balance
rows.where: The state plan website after login, the account balance on the first screen.
rows.ifMissing: The plan's quarterly statement, first page.
rows.roughly: To the nearest thousand.

rows.label: Credit report
rows.where: annualcreditreport.com, free every week from each of the three bureaus; the report lists every open account with its balance and limit.
rows.ifMissing: Your bank or card app usually shows a free credit score and a summary of accounts.
rows.roughly: Skip it; the balances you typed are enough for now.

rows.label: Credit limit
rows.where: The card app, account details, the line called credit limit or credit line; also near the top of the statement.
rows.ifMissing: The credit report lists each card's limit.
rows.roughly: Type three times the balance.

rows.label: Health plan deductible
rows.where: The health plan's summary of benefits, first page, the line called deductible for the whole family.
rows.ifMissing: The insurer's app, plan details or benefits summary.
rows.roughly: Type 2,000 for job coverage, 5,000 for a marketplace plan.

rows.label: Out-of-pocket maximum
rows.where: The same summary of benefits, the line called out-of-pocket limit, the family figure.
rows.ifMissing: The insurer's app, benefits summary.
rows.roughly: Type 8,000.

rows.label: Unemployment weekly benefit
rows.where: The determination letter from the state after you file, the line called weekly benefit amount; the state site shows it under your claim.
rows.ifMissing: The state's benefit calculator page estimates it from your last year's wages.
rows.roughly: Half your old weekly gross pay, capped at your state's maximum.

rows.label: Your 401(k) contribution rate
rows.where: The plan website, the contributions page, the percent of pay going in; also the 401(k) deduction line on your pay stub.
rows.ifMissing: Divide the retirement deduction on your pay stub by your gross pay for that stub.
rows.roughly: Type 6% if you have never changed it.

rows.label: Tax withheld so far this year
rows.where: The latest pay stub, the year-to-date column, the federal income tax line.
rows.ifMissing: Last year's W-2, box 2, is a fair guide.
rows.roughly: About 12% of gross pay so far this year.

rows.label: Cost basis of a brokerage holding
rows.where: The brokerage app, positions, the column called cost basis; the total row is the account's.
rows.ifMissing: The year-end statement or the 1099-B from the broker lists basis per lot.
rows.roughly: Type 70% of the current value.
